steps.say: This is the commonest surgical cause of vomiting in early infancy, and first born boys fill the ward. It affects 1 in 300 to 900 live births, peaks at 2 to 8 weeks, and hits males four times more often. Knowing the numbers keeps the diagnosis at the front of the mind.
steps.tx: Hypertrophic **pyloric stenosis** (thickened outlet muscle) affects 1 in **300** to **900** live births, peaks at **2** to **8** weeks, hits males **4** times more often, and **first born male** (eldest sons) infants carry the highest risk, making the **incidence** (new case rate) worth memorising.

steps.say: The outlet muscle keeps thickening until milk cannot pass, yet the baby stays hungry throughout. Circular muscle hypertrophy obstructs the gastric outlet, and absent nitric oxide synthase in pyloric tissue is implicated. Infants develop progressive projectile vomiting of nonbilious emesis yet still crave feeds.
steps.tx: Circular muscle hypertrophy obstructs the gastric outlet, absent **nitric oxide synthase** (relaxing signal enzyme) in pyloric tissue is implicated, and infants develop progressive **projectile vomiting** (forceful ejection) of **nonbilious emesis** (milk without green bile) yet still crave feeds. The hungry feeder who vomits and feeds again is showing the classic behaviour.

steps.say: An experienced hand makes the diagnosis without any scan, so examine before ordering films. A palpable epigastric olive felt by an experienced examiner is pathognomonic and needs no imaging. Visible gastric peristalsis rippling left to right across the upper abdomen supports the finding.
steps.tx: A palpable epigastric **pyloric olive** (firm mobile lump) felt by an experienced examiner is **pathognomonic** (diagnosis certain) and needs no imaging, with visible left to right **gastric peristalsis** (stomach waves) as a supporting sign in the hungry vomiting infant. Test feeds may reveal the waves rippling across the epigastrium after milk.

nodes.label: Hungry vomiting infant at 2 to 8 weeks
Feel for epigastric olive with peristalsis
Olive felt: diagnosis made, no scan

steps.say: Ultrasound confirms doubtful cases with hard cut offs that every trainee is memorising. Pyloric muscle thickness over 3 to 4 millimetres or length over 15 to 18 millimetres with functional outlet obstruction is sealing the diagnosis. Equivocal cases may use a contrast study with aspiration caution.
steps.tx: **Ultrasound** (confirmatory scan) diagnosis needs **pyloric muscle thickness** (single wall measure) over **3** to **4** mm or length over **15** to **18** mm with functional outlet obstruction. Equivocal cases may use **contrast study** (barium swallow) with aspiration caution before theatre.

vis.alt: Stomach cutaway showing hypertrophied circular muscle and elongated pyloric canal with palpable olive mass, ultrasound target sign and pyloromyotomy view.
vis.caption: Muscle over 3 to 4 mm thick or over 15 to 18 mm long with obstruction confirms the diagnosis. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Vomiting stomach acid washes away chloride and hydrogen, leaving the blood dangerously alkaline. Vomited hydrochloric acid causes hypokalemic hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis with dehydration. Anaesthesia before correction risks postoperative apnea from lost carbon dioxide drive, so resuscitate first.
steps.tx: Vomited hydrochloric acid causes hypokalemic **hypochloremia** (low chloride) **metabolic alkalosis** (alkaline blood) with dehydration, and anaesthesia before correction risks **postoperative apnea** (stopped breathing) from lost carbon dioxide drive, so fluids and salts precede any anaesthetic. Potassium falls with the chloride, so potassium replacement accompanies the fluids.

steps.say: These babies reach theatre only after salts and water are restored, because operating on alkalosis invites apnea. Resuscitation starts with a 20 millilitre per kilogram saline bolus, then D5 half saline with potassium after urine flows. Aim for bicarbonate under 30 and chloride above 95 before listing.
steps.tx: **Fluid resuscitation** (volume and salt repair) starts with a **20** mL per kg saline bolus, then D**5** half saline with **20** mEq per L potassium at **1.5** times maintenance after urine flows, aiming for **bicarbonate** (alkali reserve) under **30** and **chloride** above **95** mEq per L.

nodes.label: D5 half saline with potassium at 1.5 times maintenance
List when bicarbonate under 30 and chloride above 95

steps.say: The operation splits muscle down to bulging lining while leaving the mucosa untouched. Ramstedt Fredet pyloromyotomy splits the hypertrophied muscle to mucosal bulging with independent wall motion and no mucosal injury. Open and laparoscopic routes both work, with laparoscopy giving shorter stay and fewer wound infections.
steps.tx: **Ramstedt pyloromyotomy** (Fredet muscle splitting operation) splits the hypertrophied muscle to **mucosal bulging** (pale lining pouting) with independent wall motion and no mucosal injury, done open or by **laparoscopy** (keyhole surgery). Laparoscopy gives shorter stay and fewer wound infections. Serosal integrity is checked by insufflating air while the mucosa is watched for leaks.

vis.alt: Surgical views showing hypertrophied pylorus with bulging mucosa after myotomy beside caecum, duodenum and divided Ladd bands.
vis.caption: Pyloromyotomy splits muscle to bulging mucosa with intact lining; laparoscopy shortens stay. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Most babies vomit a little after surgery and then feed happily, so reassure before reoperating. Postoperative vomiting is common and self limited. Full thickness mucosal perforation stays under 1 percent and is commoner with laparoscopy, while emesis beyond 7 to 14 days needs a contrast study for incomplete pyloromyotomy.
steps.tx: **Postoperative emesis** (vomiting after surgery) is common and self limited, full thickness **mucosal perforation** (hole in lining) is under **1** percent and commoner with laparoscopy, and emesis beyond **7** to **14** days needs contrast study for **incomplete pyloromyotomy** (inadequate muscle split).
